SHREEJI INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTS PRIVATE LIMITED
Registered Office and Works: Plot 66, GIDC Makarpura, Vadodara 390010, Gujarat

HUMAN RESOURCES POLICY MANUAL
POLICY NO. HR-POL-007: LEAVE, ATTENDANCE AND WORK-FROM-HOME POLICY

Version: 3.2
Effective Date: 1 April 2026
Supersedes: Version 3.1 dated 1 April 2025
Policy Owner: Head - Human Resources
Approved by: Managing Director, 20 March 2026
Next Review Date: 31 March 2027

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

1.1 This policy lays down the rules for leave, attendance, late coming and work-from-home arrangements for all employees of Shreeji Industrial Products Private Limited (the "Company").

1.2 This policy applies to all confirmed employees on the rolls of the Company in the office and plant. Employees on probation are covered to the extent specifically mentioned. Contract workers engaged through contractors are governed by the terms of their contractor and the applicable labour laws.

1.3 The policy is intended to comply with the Gujarat Shops and Establishments Act, 1948 (for office staff), the Factories Act, 1948 (for plant staff), the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and the Code on Social Security, 2020, as applicable. If any law gives a higher benefit, the law shall prevail.

2. WORKING HOURS AND ATTENDANCE

2.1 Office staff (Monday to Friday and alternate Saturdays): 9:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., with a lunch break of 45 minutes. The second and fourth Saturday of each month are holidays for office staff.

2.2 Plant staff work in three shifts: Shift A 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., Shift B 2:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m., and Shift C 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. Each plant employee is entitled to one weekly off, which is Sunday unless the shift roster says otherwise.

2.3 Attendance is recorded through the biometric system at the gate and the Employee Self-Service portal. Every employee must mark attendance on arrival and departure. Failure to mark attendance, without a valid reason, will be treated as absence.

2.4 Attendance regularisation (for missed punches, biometric failure or official visits) must be applied for on the portal within three (3) working days of the date concerned, and approved by the reporting manager. A maximum of three (3) regularisations is allowed per employee per month.

3. LEAVE ENTITLEMENT

3.1 The leave year is the calendar year, 1 January to 31 December. The leave entitlements for a full year are set out in the following table.

Leave type                   | Entitlement per year          | Accrual / credit                | Carry forward                      | Encashment
Casual Leave (CL)            | 8 days                        | Credited on 1 January           | Not allowed; lapses on 31 Dec      | Not allowed
Sick Leave (SL)              | 8 days                        | Credited on 1 January           | Not allowed; lapses on 31 Dec      | Not allowed
Earned Leave / Privilege (EL)| 18 days                       | 1.5 days per month of service   | Up to 30 days maximum accumulation | Allowed, see 3.6
Maternity Leave              | 26 weeks (first two children) | On request, with medical proof  | Not applicable                     | Not applicable
Paternity Leave              | 5 working days                | Within 3 months of the birth    | Not allowed                        | Not allowed
Marriage Leave               | 3 working days                | Once in service, own marriage   | Not applicable                     | Not allowed
Bereavement Leave            | 3 working days                | Immediate family member         | Not applicable                     | Not allowed
Compensatory Off             | 1 day for 1 day worked        | On holiday or weekly off work   | Must be availed within 30 days     | Not allowed

3.2 Casual leave shall not be taken for more than three (3) consecutive days at a time. Casual leave cannot be combined with earned leave.

3.3 Sick leave of more than two (2) consecutive days must be supported by a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner, submitted within three (3) days of resuming duty. Sick leave of five (5) or more days requires a fitness certificate before resumption.

3.4 Earned leave may be applied for a minimum of two (2) days and requires seven (7) calendar days' prior notice if applied for more than three (3) days. An employee may carry forward earned leave so that the accumulated balance does not exceed thirty (30) days. Any balance above thirty (30) days at the end of the leave year will lapse, except for employees in the plant, who may carry forward up to forty-five (45) days.

3.5 New joinees are credited with leave on a pro-rata basis from the date of joining: casual and sick leave in proportion to the remaining months of the year, and earned leave at 1.5 days per month from the month of confirmation. Employees on probation may avail casual and sick leave but not earned leave.

3.6 Encashment of earned leave is allowed at the time of separation (resignation, retirement or termination other than for misconduct) for a maximum of fifteen (15) days at the rate of one day's basic salary divided by 26. In addition, an employee may encash up to ten (10) days of earned leave once in a leave year in the month of December, provided that a minimum balance of ten (10) days remains after such encashment.

3.7 Maternity leave of 26 weeks is available to women employees for the first two surviving children, of which not more than 8 weeks may precede the expected date of delivery. For the third child and thereafter, 12 weeks of maternity leave are available. The Company will provide a crèche facility under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and a work-from-home option for up to eight (8) weeks following the maternity leave, if the nature of work permits.

3.8 Holidays: The Company observes twelve (12) paid holidays in a year, notified by the Human Resources department in December of the preceding year. The holiday list for 2026 includes Republic Day (26 January), Holi (4 March), Independence Day (15 August), Ganesh Chaturthi (14 September), Gandhi Jayanti (2 October), Dussehra (20 October), Diwali (8 November), Gujarati New Year / Vikram Samvat (10 November) and Christmas Day (25 December). Employees may choose three (3) optional holidays from a list of eight (8), which must be applied for at least five (5) days in advance.

3.9 Leave Without Pay (LWP): Where an employee has no leave balance, or is absent without approval, the period of absence shall be treated as leave without pay, and salary shall be deducted at one thirtieth (1/30) of the monthly gross salary for each day. Absence of more than five (5) consecutive working days without information shall be treated as abandonment of service after a notice has been sent.

3.10 Sandwich rule: Holidays and weekly offs that fall between two periods of leave of the same type taken without a break shall be counted as leave, for casual leave and sick leave only.

4. APPLYING FOR AND APPROVING LEAVE

4.1 All leave must be applied for on the Employee Self-Service portal. In an emergency, an employee must inform the reporting manager by phone or message before 10:00 a.m. on the day of absence, and apply for leave on the portal within two (2) days of resuming duty.

4.2 The reporting manager shall approve or reject the leave application within two (2) working days. Leave shall be deemed to be approved only if the manager approves it on the portal. Leave may be refused or curtailed, with reasons, where the exigencies of work so require, except for maternity leave, which is a statutory right.

4.3 A leave encashment or carry-forward balance shall be reconciled by the Human Resources department by 15 January of every year, and a statement shall be placed on the portal.

5. LATE COMING AND EARLY GOING

5.1 A grace period of fifteen (15) minutes is allowed for reporting after the start time of the shift or the office, up to a maximum of three (3) times in a calendar month. The grace period is not available on the 4th and subsequent occasions.

5.2 The following consequences apply to late coming beyond the grace permitted:

Late coming occasions in a month | Consequence
Up to 3 occasions of up to 15 minutes | No deduction (grace)
4th occasion in the month | Half day of casual leave deducted
5th to 6th occasion | Half day of casual leave deducted for each occasion
7th occasion and above | Full day of pay deducted for each two (2) occasions; counselling letter issued
Arrival after 11:00 a.m. (office) or after 2 hours from the shift start (plant) without prior approval | Treated as half day absent
More than 3 months in a row with 4 or more late marks | Written warning, to be placed in the personal file

5.3 Early departure of more than 30 minutes before the end of the shift without prior approval shall be treated as a half-day absence.

5.4 Where the casual leave balance is nil, the deduction shall be made as leave without pay in accordance with Clause 3.9.

6. WORK FROM HOME (WFH)

6.1 Work from home is available to confirmed office-based employees in the grade of Executive and above, whose roles can be performed remotely, subject to the approval of the department head. It is not available to plant staff, security, stores, dispatch, maintenance and any employee whose job requires physical presence.

6.2 An eligible employee may work from home for a maximum of two (2) days in a week and eight (8) days in a calendar month. WFH days cannot be combined with a weekly off or holiday to extend a period of absence, and the WFH days shall not be carried over.

6.3 The application for WFH must be made on the portal by 6:00 p.m. on the previous working day, and the reporting manager's approval must be obtained. In an emergency, same-day WFH is allowed with the manager's consent given by message before 9:30 a.m.

6.4 The WFH employee must be available on the Company's messaging platform during core hours of 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., attend all meetings scheduled by video call, and respond to calls within thirty (30) minutes. Failure to do so shall result in the WFH day being treated as casual leave of half a day.

6.5 The employee shall use the Company's VPN and approved devices only, and shall not store Company data on personal devices or personal cloud storage. The Company reserves the right to withdraw WFH privileges at any time.

6.6 WFH is not available during the first six (6) months of employment, during a performance improvement plan, or in the last month of the notice period.

7. EXTENDED ABSENCE, MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS

7.1 An employee who wishes to take unpaid leave of more than fifteen (15) days, or a sabbatical for study, may apply to the Head - Human Resources at least 60 days in advance. Such leave may be granted for a maximum of three (3) months at the discretion of the Managing Director.

7.2 Leave taken during the notice period shall extend the notice period by the number of days of leave availed, unless the Company agrees otherwise in writing.

7.3 Misrepresentation of the reason for leave, the submission of a false medical certificate, or abuse of the WFH facility shall be treated as misconduct and shall be dealt with under the Standing Orders and the disciplinary policy.

7.4 Queries relating to this policy may be addressed to the Human Resources department at hr@shreeji-industrial.example. The Managing Director has the power to relax any provision of this policy in exceptional cases for reasons recorded in writing.

REVISION HISTORY

Version 3.0 - 1 April 2024 - Introduction of WFH provisions
Version 3.1 - 1 April 2025 - Increase of EL accumulation limit from 24 to 30 days
Version 3.2 - 1 April 2026 - Revision of late-coming rules; encashment of 10 days in December introduced
